context.requirement_text: REQ-187 -- Wire TIMER nodes into the engine -- arm on token arrival, cancel on completion/cancellation (SCH-01/SCH-03, closes the cancel_pending_timers stub). Connects REQ-186's timers core to the instance engine, closing three named, already-documented stubs: (a) transition.ex L294's catch-all dispatch branch, which today returns {:error, {:node_type_not_yet_implemented, :TIMER, node_id}} for every TIMER node; (b) task_activation.ex L338-339's cancel_pending_timers/2, an explicit no-op; (c) engine.ex L234-242's recorded cancel_instance/3 deferral (timer half only -- REQ-056's SERVICE_TASK HTTP-abort half stays deferred). SCOPE: (1) a token arriving at a :TIMER node arms a timer via REQ-186's create/2 with fire_at = arrival time + the node's duration_iso8601 attribute (already validated at definition time by CHK-12), persisted in the SAME transaction as the state-transition event; the token waits at the node rather than advancing. (2) when the poller fires a timer, the instance advances from the TIMER node along its outgoing edge; a timer armed with fire_at already <= now is due immediately on the next poll and must NOT be special-cased into firing inline inside the arming transaction. (3) cancellation: replace cancel_pending_timers/2's no-op with a real status-guarded update setting every PENDING timer for that instance to cancelled (cancelled_at + cancel_reason), on the caller-supplied repo/prefix; add the equivalent call inside cancel_instance/3's own transaction. (4) PURITY: transition/3 must RETURN a description of the timer to be armed (extending its existing pending_event() return shape) and never call Repo itself; the impure caller persists it. SCH-03's concurrency edge case must hold: a fired timer is never touched by a later cancellation, and no pending timer of a terminal instance is ever fired by a later poll. NOT IN THIS REQUIREMENT: no route/controller; no recurrence or escalation timers (REQ-188); no change to REQ-056's SERVICE_TASK dispatch.
context.note: The design (lib/letflow/design/req187-timer-engine-wiring.md) passed CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's Step 1b gate clean -- see handoffs/WF02-REQ187-20260829/step-01b-code-design-validator.json's result.summary for the full independent re-derivation (purity constraint confirmed genuine against transition.ex's real pending_event() type and dispatch_node/4 clauses; the fire-path SAVEPOINT nesting confirmed sound against Ecto.Multi's real 4-tuple failure shape and Postgres's real SAVEPOINT support; the cancel_instance/3 lock-ordering deadlock hazard and its fix independently verified against the real run_cancel_instance/5 Multi order at engine.ex:2470-2504). Implement the design as written, with ONE addition folded in below (from the validator's own resolution of the design's open question 3, not left as an open question for you to adjudicate) and TWO citation corrections to be aware of (do not let them change what you build, only what precedent you rely on).

task.description: Implement REQ-187 strictly per the APPROVED design at lib/letflow/design/req187-timer-engine-wiring.md. Read the full design doc before writing any code -- follow its exact module/function layout, names, and @spec shapes; do not improvise alternate names or signatures. Six files change, exactly as the design's §11 table lists: lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex (new pending_event()/transition_event()/transition_error() variants; new dispatch_timer_arrival/3, dispatch_timer_fired/4; catch-all comment corrected to name only :SERVICE_TASK; moduledoc purity-section note naming the extended shape -- NO Repo/clock call added anywhere in this file), lib/letflow/definitions/graph.ex (new public parse_iso8601_duration/1, sharing valid_iso8601_duration?/1's token-scanning helpers, unit-to-seconds table: Y=365d, M(date)=30d, W=7d, D=1d, H=3600s, M(time)=60s, S=1s), lib/letflow/engine.ex (new prepare_timer_arms/4, build_timer_arms_multi/4, advance_after_timer_fired/3 per §8's 4 steps; persist/11 and build_complete_task_tail_multi/6 each gain one Multi.merge/2 step per §3.2; finalize_instance_projection/5's :completed clause's existing cancel_pending_timers call updated in place, line position UNMOVED; run_cancel_instance/5 gains :timer_cancellations between the EXISTING :open_tasks and :instance_projection steps -- this exact placement is load-bearing for the deadlock fix, do not move it elsewhere), lib/letflow/engine/task_activation.ex (cancel_pending_timers/2 -> /5 per §5.1's exact @spec and body), lib/letflow/scheduler.ex (do_fire/2 gains one new with-clause calling Letflow.Engine.advance_after_timer_fired/3 per §7.1; attempt_fire/2 gains one new case clause per §7.2, matched BEFORE the existing {:error, _reason} -> safe_record_fire_failure(...) catch-all), lib/letflow/engine/reconstruction.ex (new apply_event/3 clause for "TIMER_FIRED" per §9, mirroring the existing "TASK_COMPLETED" clause's shape, not "SUB_PROCESS_COMPLETED"'s). REQUIRED ADDITION beyond the design's literal text (CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's resolution of the design's own open question 3, §13 item 3): prepare_timer_arms/4 (§3.1) must add a defensive check -- if filtering pending_events for {:timer_armed, ...} yields MORE THAN ONE entry, return {:error, {:multiple_timers_in_one_hop_chain_not_supported, node_ids}} (add this to prepare_timer_arms/4's own error union in its @spec) instead of proceeding to build_timer_arms_multi/4. Rationale: Scheduler.create/2's Multi branch hardcodes the literal step name :scheduler_timer (verified at scheduler.ex:94, Multi.insert(multi, :scheduler_timer, ...)); calling it twice in the same Multi RAISES (Ecto.Multi raises a bare RuntimeError on a duplicate step name, verified at deps/ecto/lib/ecto/multi.ex:750), which is not a typed error this codebase's totality discipline tolerates. This scenario is reachable today because :PARALLEL_GATEWAY already has a real dispatch clause (transition.ex:265-272) -- a split feeding two branches that each land on a :TIMER node in the same advance_until_stable/4 hop-chain is not excluded by REQ-187's scope. This guard turns a latent crash into a graceful, typed failure; do not attempt to actually support multiple simultaneous timers per hop-chain (that requires widening Scheduler.create/2's Multi API to accept a caller-supplied step name, which is explicitly out of scope here -- the guard is the whole fix). TWO non-blocking citation corrections from the validator's own re-derivation, for your awareness only (do not change your implementation because of these, only don't rely on the cited precedent as a cross-check): (1) design §3.2's subheading 'No Ecto.Multi name collision:' is mislabeled -- ignore the heading, follow §13 item 3's correct description of the actual risk (addressed above); (2) design §3.2 claims the new timer-arm Multi.merge step's 'before :event' placement matches where append_sub_process_children_creation_multi/6 already sits in build_complete_task_tail_multi/6 -- this is false (that function actually calls append_sub_process_children_creation_multi/6 AFTER :event and after :projection, engine.ex:2004-2028); follow the design's explicit instruction (place the new step after :token_reconciliation and before :event) rather than the incorrect precedent claim -- this placement is still correct because :token_reconciliation (engine.ex:2166) already resolves the real TokenRecord ids the new step's id_map needs, before :event ever runs, and Ecto.Multi's own all-or-nothing semantics (not step order) is what actually satisfies AC2. Follow lib/letflow/design/req187-timer-engine-wiring.md's §1-§10 for every other detail (dispatch clause bodies, the arm_attrs shape, the Multi step ordering rationale, the reconciliation/reconstruction wiring) -- it is unambiguous and does not need further judgment calls beyond the one addition named above.
acceptance_criteria: a definition containing a TIMER node with a valid duration_iso8601 starts an instance whose token reaches that node and arms exactly one timers row with status 'pending' and fire_at equal to the arrival timestamp plus the parsed duration -- replacing the {:error, {:node_type_not_yet_implemented, :TIMER, _}} that transition.ex L294 returns today, asserted by a test that would have failed before this requirement
the timer row and the state-transition event are written in ONE transaction: a test that forces the event append to fail leaves NO timers row behind
when the timer fires, the instance advances along the TIMER node's outgoing edge and the token is no longer at the TIMER node

completing an instance sets every one of its PENDING timers to 'cancelled' with cancelled_at set, via the existing TaskActivation.cancel_pending_timers/2 call site in engine.ex -- which is still called from the same position inside the completion transaction (confirmed by git diff showing the call site itself unmoved)

cancelling an instance via Letflow.Engine.cancel_instance/3 likewise cancels its PENDING timers in the same transaction, and a test forcing that transaction to roll back leaves the timers still 'pending'

a timer whose status is already 'fired' is NOT changed by a subsequent instance cancellation (SCH-03's stated edge case), and no PENDING timer belonging to a CANCELLED or COMPLETED instance is ever fired by a later poll -- two explicit tests

lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex contains no Letflow.Repo call after this change, confirmed by the same grep its moduledoc already documents for purity, and the moduledoc names which return shape was extended to carry the timer-arming description instead
no route or controller file is added or modified, confirmed by git diff --stat scoped to this requirement's commits
mix test and mix compile --warnings-as-errors both pass with real output quoted
